shorts.title: What you will learn: Multiple inheritance
shorts.hook: Two parents can make one question ambiguous.
shorts.script: Two parents can make one question ambiguous. Today a class gets two parents. This is powerful, but it brings the famous diamond problem. C plus plus lets a class inherit from more than one base. List them with commas. If both bases have a member with the same name, a call is ambiguous. You must say which one you mean. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Multiple inheritance.

shorts.title: Multiple inheritance in one minute
shorts.hook: C plus plus lets a class inherit from more than one base.
shorts.script: C plus plus lets a class inherit from more than one base. List them with commas. If both bases have a member with the same name, a call is ambiguous. You must say which one you mean. The diamond problem appears when two bases share one grandparent. Then the object holds two copies of it. Virtual inheritance keeps only one. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Multiple inheritance in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: Animal has one member, legs. The word virtual tells the compiler to share one Animal part. Swimmer does the same. Duck has only one Animal part. So the name legs is not ambiguous. We can use it directly. The output is four. The program prints four. A class can inherit from several bases. Equal member names in two bases make a call ambiguous. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: An ambiguous member
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. Both bases have a hello function. The call on C says hello, and the compiler says the request for hello is ambiguous. It cannot guess. Write the base name and two colons to choose. Both bases offer hello, so the compiler cannot guess. Write the name of the base and two colons to choose one. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: AN AMBIGUOUS MEMBER
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: An ambiguous member.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: A diamond is forever. So is the ambiguity, until you add virtual.
shorts.script: A diamond is forever. So is the ambiguity, until you add virtual. Make two base classes with the same function name. Inherit from both, and call each version. Write your answer in the comments. A class can inherit from several bases. Equal member names in two bases make a call ambiguous. The diamond gives two copies of the grandparent. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
